current.text: Jakob Poeltl is projected to start at center. Murray-Boyles is expected to come off the bench but close games for the Raptors.
Experts expect 25 or more minutes a game, at least three more than last season. One preview expects close to 30 minutes as a super sub.
Sandro Mamukelashvili is no longer competing for his minutes, and his thumb injury from last season is behind him.
Toronto is not deep after its top seven, and Poeltl is the only seven-footer on the roster.
His usage is projected to rise from about 15% to about 18%. He is expected to have the ball more and score more. One expert predicts a top three Sixth Man of the Year finish.
He could average about 12 points, 7 rebounds and 1.5 blocks.
Experts see him as roughly a top 100 player as a baseline, with a range of top 100 to 120.
If he plays 30 minutes a game, he could be a top 70 player.
His draft cost is around ADP 115 to the 120s.
He is a good late flyer. He has enough standalone value for rounds 10 to 11 even if you already have Poeltl, and one expert would draft him ahead of Poeltl.
The Raptors have 15 back-to-backs, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: His three-point shot is a long-term project. It looked fine on low volume but is not reliable yet. He makes very few threes, which is his weakest category for his position.
He is 6'7 and plays center in small, switchable lineups. Toronto's rebounding and rim protection held steady or improved with him at center.

note: Yahoo prices him at 3 USD (rank 111) and ESPN at 0 USD (rank 174). Experts see a top 100 baseline and top 70 upside at 30 minutes, so he is a good 1 to 3 USD end-of-auction flyer in our 144-player draft. He adds FG% (58% on low volume), blocks and steals with few turnovers, fits punt 3PM builds best, and his 66% FT% is a minor drag. Early in the season, check that he closes games and plays 25 or more minutes behind Poeltl.
